A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same deCIFer research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original NOMA and CHILI-100K evaluations, conditioning ablations, perturbation experiments and analyses of generated structures.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds four CSP benchmark comparisons and an unconditioned-model comparison on CHILI-100K.

M1.justification: The PXRD encoder, conditioning-token insertion, autoregressive objective, transformer architecture, sequence packing and attention isolation are unchanged. The additional benchmarks do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates NOMA and CHILI-100K. v3 retains both and adds Perov-5, Carbon-24, MP-20 and MPTS-52 evaluations (Table 1), substantially broadening benchmark coverage, including targeted perovskite and carbon structure prediction.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's U-deCIFer comparator, v3 reports comparisons with CDVAE, DiffCSP and CrystaLLM-small/large in Table 1. It also adds U-deCIFer to the CHILI-100K comparison in Table 2. Appendix A.11 acknowledges that the external baselines receive different conditioning information.

E3.justification: v3 removes Wasserstein distance from evaluation and introduces aligned atomic RMSE for the new benchmarks, using reported official DiffCSP train-test splits and one generated structure per composition. The original model settings and StructureMatcher tolerances remain unchanged. Changed CHILI-100K plot counts are unexplained and do not establish a specific revised sampling protocol.

E4.justification: v3 adds an OOD conditioning ablation against U-deCIFer on CHILI-100K and expands its perturbation distributions from three to seven scenarios. Existing PCA and 16K-generation analyses remain, but the latter loses its explicit worst-case examples. These extend and revise the established analyses.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 6 specifies 100 generations per illustrative case and selection of the median; v3's corresponding illustrations omit this repeated-sampling information. Mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting and the stated 16K-generation analysis remain. Neither version reports training-seed uncertainty or significance tests.

E6.justification: v3 adds benchmark MR/RMSE results and CHILI-100K U-deCIFer results: Rwp 0.96 ± 0.32 and MR 25.92%, versus retained deCIFer values of 0.70 ± 0.37 and 37.34%. Original aggregate scores remain, while WD results disappear. The consistency figure revises composition labels and removes worst-case results. CHILI-100K crystal-system results also change, with unexplained count increases.

T1.justification: The conditional likelihood, attention-isolation formulation, PXRD simulation equations and match-rate definition are retained. Removing the standard Wasserstein-distance formula accompanies the evaluation-metric removal; there is no substantive revision to theoretical reasoning, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central PXRD-conditioned CIF-generation contribution and approximately 94% match-rate claim remain. v3 drops the assertion that the training structures are unique, adds external comparisons to its contributions, and narrows the conclusion to useful starting structures requiring downstream verification.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion of homometric ambiguity, dependence on informative diffraction signals, possible conflicts between conditioning and learned composition priors, and weaknesses of symmetry-bin stratification (Section 6 and Appendices A.9/A.11). These materially qualify applicability beyond v1's discussion of robustness, overlap and complementary metrics.

D1.justification: Architecture, training hyperparameters, hardware description and code access remain essentially unchanged. However, v3 omits v1's explicit 90%/7.5%/2.5% NOMA split proportions; the relocated stratification description does not restore them. This reduces reproducibility information without establishing that the actual split changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds CDVAE and literature supporting the new benchmarks, dataset-bias discussion and homometric limitations. The central positioning against composition-conditioned CSP and the existing LLM/diffusion research context remain, so this extends rather than replaces the research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative: related work becomes a numbered section with topical paragraphs, evaluation moves into the experimental section, results begin with external comparisons, and future work moves to the appendix. The introduction, discussion, conclusion and numerous captions are rewritten.

P2.justification: v3 merges plots and tables into Figures 3 and 5, combines crystal-system analysis with examples in Figure 4, redesigns the consistency figure horizontally, and relocates the attention visualization to the appendix. It also adds comparison tables and removes WD panels throughout. These are extensive display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's mainly internal comparisons, v3 supplies useful external benchmark context, an OOD conditioning control and clearer physical and practical limitations. These improve assessment of the method's scope. The net gain is limited by unequal conditioning in the new comparisons, lost WD and split reporting, and unresolved inconsistencies: Carbon-24 superiority wording overlooks deCIFer's worse RMSE than CrystaLLM-small, while Figure 15's CHILI-100K counts exceed the still-stated 8,201-structure dataset without explanation.
